summary: Pre-market: the 10-year Treasury completed the break to 5.00 from 4.97, the 100.0th percentile of its history, and the 10-year real rate rose to 2.62 from 2.60, also at the 100.0th percentile, so the discount-rate block now sits at the top of its entire distribution as the market digests a Fed that hiked 25 basis points and signalled more. The composite eased 0.38 to 47.72 with the regime still goldilocks at a model confidence of 0.9268, so the framework again declines to score the episode as a risk event: volatility at 29.0 and liquidity and credit at 36.98 stay benign while only the macro block at 63.77 approaches stress. What genuinely changed overnight is that the long end rose while breakevens fell, the 5-year to 2.31 from 2.35 and the 10-year to 2.33 from 2.38, so this is a real-rate repricing rather than an inflation repricing. Reverse repo balances also snapped back to 5.375 from 0.7, refilling a facility that had been effectively drained, with SOFR at 3.64. The last completed US session rewarded AI hardware and punished software: AI infrastructure gained 2.9662 percent, networking 2.7137 percent and data centers 2.1401 percent, while FinTech lost 1.9217 percent and AI software 0.9611 percent. The tracked A-share AI panel then closed 10 of 11 names lower, led by 688825.sh at -2.9583 percent, the mirror image of the previous session. Breadth remains the structural problem with the new-highs ratio at 0.0 out of 155 names and 0.5355 above the 200-day average. Credit is now the one input that moved with the tape as high-yield spreads widened to 2.76 from 2.71, while VIX at 17.2 and bitcoin at 76274 both refuse to confirm.

top_risk_drivers.claim: The discount-rate block sits at the top of its distribution: the 10-year Treasury at 5.00 and the 10-year real rate at 2.62 are both at the 100.0th percentile, contributing 5.00 weighted points each and 10.00 together before the hike transmits.

The front end added to the move after the 25 basis point hike: the 2-year rose to 4.67 from 4.65 and the curve at 0.33 steepened, with swap pricing at 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63, so the market is repricing a cycle rather than a single meeting.

Credit finally moved with the tape: high-yield spreads widened to 2.76 from 2.71 while investment-grade held at 0.80, so the credit channel is now the one input that confirms the rate move even though the model's widening signal stays untriggered at 2.76 against a trigger of 4.

Breadth is still the structural problem: the new-highs ratio is 0.0 out of 155 names, 0.5355 sit above the 200-day average and small caps lag by 3.2895 percentage points, which keeps breadth the fifth-heaviest contribution at 3.3283 points.

Cross-asset confirmation is flat at 0.5 with 5 of 10 signals triggered but remains the single heaviest contribution at 7.50 weighted points, carried by the dollar at 118.2126 and real rates at 2.62, with bitcoin at 76274 leaving the risk-off signal untriggered.

supporting_signals.claim: The long end rose on real rates rather than inflation: the 5-year breakeven fell to 2.31 from 2.35 and the 10-year to 2.33 from 2.38, so the tightening is being transmitted through real yields while headline CPI at 3.35302 and core at 2.44616 keep the price backdrop mixed.

The last completed US session split the AI complex rather than de-rating it: AI infrastructure gained 2.9662 percent, networking 2.7137 percent and data centers 2.1401 percent, while FinTech lost 1.9217 percent and AI software 0.9611 percent — hardware was bought, software was offered.

The A-share AI panel did not mirror the US hardware bid: 10 of 11 tracked names closed lower, led by 688825.sh at -2.9583 percent, 688008.sh at -2.7815 percent and 600584.sh at -2.5881 percent, with 300223.sz the only gainer at 0.7459 percent.

Policy delivered and the market is now pricing above it: the FOMC statement and its economic projections were released with swap pricing at 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63, so the forward path is the live variable rather than the level.

contradicting_signals.claim: The framework barely registered the event: the composite eased 0.38 to 47.72 with the regime still goldilocks at a model confidence of 0.9268, so the model has not classified the rate break as a risk event.

Volatility and investment-grade credit are calm while only the discount rate is stressed: VIX sits at 17.2 in the 45.63rd percentile, realized volatility is 8.6543 and investment-grade spreads hold at 0.80.

The funding cushion refilled rather than drained: reverse repo balances rebounded to 5.375 from 0.7 while reserves held at 2991310 and SOFR moved to 3.64 from 3.62, so there is no funding stress behind the rate move.
Crypto advanced through the rate shock instead of hedging it: bitcoin at 76274, ethereum at 2430.45 and solana at 99.65, leaving the model's bitcoin-down signal untriggered.

what_changed_today: The 10-year Treasury completed the break to 5.00 from 4.97 at the 100.0th percentile and the 10-year real rate rose to 2.62 from 2.60, also at the 100.0th percentile.
Breakevens fell against the nominal move: the 5-year to 2.31 from 2.35 and the 10-year to 2.33 from 2.38, confirming a real-rate repricing.
Reverse repo balances rebounded to 5.375 from 0.7 while reserves held at 2991310 and SOFR moved to 3.64 from 3.62.
The composite eased 0.38 to 47.72 with the regime unchanged at goldilocks and model confidence at 0.9268.
The tracked A-share AI panel closed 10 of 11 names lower led by 688825.sh at -2.9583 percent, reversing the previous session's uniform advance.
Overnight equity futures pointed to a rebound after the Fed sell-off, and the Bank of England decides today with UK inflation at 3.1 percent, above forecast.
watch_next: Whether the 10-year holds at 5.00 or extends, and whether the 2-year follows from 4.67.
Whether breakevens keep falling from 2.31 and 2.33, which would confirm real-rate tightening rather than an inflation impulse.
Whether the reverse repo rebound to 5.375 holds or reverses, with SOFR at 3.64 and reserves at 2991310.
Breadth repair: whether the new-highs ratio moves off 0.0 out of 155 names and 0.5355 above the 200-day average improves, with small caps 3.2895 points behind.

The Bank of England decision today, then the FOMC meeting on 2026-09-28 and the personal income and outlays and GDP releases on 2026-09-30, plus A-share follow-through after 10 of 11 tracked names closed lower.

bull_case.title: Bull case: the real-rate shock is a level shift the tape can absorb
points: Inflation compensation is falling, not rising: the 5-year breakeven at 2.31 from 2.35 and core CPI at 2.44616 from 2.46652 suggest the tightening is doing its job rather than chasing prices.

Stress is contained: VIX at 17.2 in the 45.63rd percentile, realized volatility at 8.6543 and high-yield spreads at 2.76 in the 20.23rd percentile, far below the 4 trigger for the model's widening signal.
The AI hardware complex was bought through the shock: AI infrastructure at 2.9662 percent, networking at 2.7137 percent and data centers at 2.1401 percent.
The funding cushion refilled to 5.375 from 0.7 with SOFR at 3.64, so this is not a liquidity event.

base_case.title: Base case: caution holds while the discount rate resets
points: The composite stays near 47.72 with the regime at goldilocks and confidence at 0.9268, so the caution level persists without escalating.
The macro block at 63.77 remains the binding constraint as long as the 10-year holds at 5.00 and the real rate at 2.62.
Breadth stays impaired with the new-highs ratio at 0.0 out of 155 names and 0.5355 above the 200-day average.

bear_case.title: Bear case: the 10-year at 5.00 breaks the equity multiple
points: Both the 10-year at 5.00 and the real rate at 2.62 sit at the 100.0th percentile, so there is no historical cushion above this level.
The aggravating drivers are already in place: the new-highs ratio at 0.0, small caps 3.2895 points behind and semis 15.5793 points behind.
Credit is the channel to watch: high-yield spreads widened to 2.76 from 2.71, and a move toward the 4 trigger level would flip the model's confirmation signal.
Swap pricing at 4.16 against an effective funds rate of 3.63 leaves the front end exposed to another hike.
